To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there has been significant change in industrial relations in the public sector in Australia, that there are two emerging models for wage determination in this sector, one a collectivist, two-tiered model, and the other a decentralized model, and that the implications of these models for the public sector workforce are complex and varied.
there are two models of public service wage determination emerging in Australia.

(a) the two-tiered wage-fixing system has resulted in the public sector becoming more like the private sector in terms of the way wages are set; (b) the two-tier model has resulted in a more fragmented system of public service wage-fixing, with the result that wage outcomes are less predictable; and (c) the two-tier system is not necessarily the best model of public service wage determination.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the impact on wage-fixing systems of: the shift from centralised wage fixing to enterprise bargaining in the private sector; the introduction of a federal system of industrial relations; and, in some jurisdictions, the introduction of individual contracts.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current public sector industrial relations system has been designed to provide a framework for the development of individual agreements.
the two-tiered model is a more effective way of dealing with public sector wage-fixers.
the two-tiered model is more likely to lead to greater wage equality, while the de-collectivist individual model is more likely, in practice, to lead to wage dispersion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single model of wage-fixing in the Australian public services.
the current systems of public sector wage determination have a significant impact on public sector workers and on the quality of public services.
the Australian public sector has been subject to a wide variety of wage-fixing mechanisms and the future is uncertain.
